messages.author: 9869e52e9a4f7d9a
messages.subject: Replicating simple random effects models
parts:
Hi there,

I'm trying to replicate a simple, classical, random intercept model based off of something I would run in lme4:

Here's my replication code:
pacman::p_load(INLA, lme4)
data_use <- sleepstudy
mod1 <- lmer(Reaction ~ 1 + Days + (1 | Subject), sleepstudy)
print(mod1)

mod2 <- inla(formula = Reaction ~ 1 + Days + f(Subject, model = 'iid'), data = sleepstudy)
summary(mod2)

If I extract out the random effect estimates from each model (the estimates of the FEs are very similar), here's how they look:
> head(ranef(mod1)$Subject)
    (Intercept)
308   40.783710
309  -77.849554
310  -63.108567
330    4.406442
331   10.216189
332    8.221238
> head(mod2$summary.random[[1]][,1:2])
   ID          mean
1 308  2.624762e-04
2 309 -5.010247e-04
3 310 -4.061546e-04
4 330  2.835913e-05
5 331  6.574954e-05
6 332  5.291041e-05

> fixef(mod1)
(Intercept)        Days 
  251.40510    10.46729 
> head(mod2$summary.fixed[,1:2])
                mean       sd
(Intercept) 251.4775 6.620995
Days         10.4512 1.239954

My questions are, in order to run/replicate a simple random intercept model in INLA:

1) Do I need to do any ad-hoc transformation for the estimates of the random effects to reflect that of a classical random effect model?

2) Could this simple example be replicated using the 'z' model instead of 'iid'? I was a bit confused on how to implement 'z', and I imagine that in the future, I may have complicated RE structures where all the groups aren't IID, and so I might have to use something flexible?


Thanks!!

Nafis

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Replicating simple random effects models
parts:
Both models have the same math. The main difference is that INLA
estimates a high precision/low variance for the random effect with
default prior. Using a more informative prior yields similar results
as lme4

library(INLA)
library(lme4)
sleepstudy$ID <- as.factor(sleepstudy$Subject)
mod1 <- lmer(Reaction ~ 1 + Days + (1 | Subject), sleepstudy)
mod2 <- inla(
Reaction ~ 1 + Days + f(Subject, model = 'iid'),

data = sleepstudy,
control.compute = list(waic = TRUE)
)
mod3 <- inla(
Reaction ~ 1 + Days +

f(Subject, model = 'iid', hyper = list(theta = list(param = c(1, 1e-3)))),
data = sleepstudy,
control.compute = list(waic = TRUE)
)
par(mfrow = c(2, 1))
plot(
ranef(mod1)$Subject[, 1],
mod2$summary.random$Subject$mean
)
abline(a = 0, b = 1)
plot(
ranef(mod1)$Subject[, 1],
mod3$summary.random$Subject$mean
)
abline(a = 0, b = 1)

Best regards,

messages.author: 8dbb28b015bb7762
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Replicating simple random effects models
parts:
Yes, the problem is in the priors. Yet, the estimates of variances from Thierry are still off from lme4.

You also need to adjust the prior for the precision of the observations (i.e. the residual variance).

The default priors used by INLA are no good here (they are designed for data varying around 1. Your data varies in the hundreds (sd ~ 57). Yet, the default priors for the standard deviations of the data and the Subject effect have 98% of its mass between 0.0034 and 0.069!!!

If instead you adjust your priors so that the 98% central quantile is, for example, between 10 and 200, then you get very similar (point) estimates.

I've put together some code demonstrating this in detail, if you are interested [1]

Best

        ƒacu.-

[1] https://gist.github.com/famuvie/639e3aaebba1ba0b1862215b02cccabe

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Replicating simple random effects models
parts:
I didn't test it, but it should be a matter of computing the corresponding indicator matrix Z (a.k.a. complete disjunctive table) from your iid variable.

E.g., if your variable is "individual", make it a factor and do

Zmat <- model.matrix(~ 0 + individual, data = dat)

You can use that to feed your "z" model.
